question.text: Before a stock exchange can start trading in any new derivative contract, it must:

answer.text: Obtain prior approval from SEBI before commencing trading in the derivative contract
Get approval only from the exchange's own board
Launch the contract first and inform SEBI later
Obtain approval from RBI since derivatives involve financial risk

explanation.text: The Logic: The workbook states that an exchange must obtain prior SEBI approval before starting trading in any derivative contract. The same regulatory thread also requires SEBI approval before an exchange changes expiry days for existing derivative contracts. The Trap: Board-only approval or self-regulation does not satisfy the requirement; prior SEBI approval is needed before launch. RBI is not the approving authority for exchange-traded equity derivatives. Note: Rule to remember: prior SEBI approval is required before an exchange begins trading in any derivative contract.
